Overview

The Problem

Distracted driving and color vision deficiency (CVD) are two independent factors that can degrade a driver's ability to accurately perceive and respond to traffic signals. Shortened glance time reduces the window available to process visual information, while deuteranomaly and deuteranopia alter the perceived color of red and green signals, making them harder to distinguish.

This experiment was designed to quantify the threshold effects of both variables: how severe does deuteranomaly need to be before drivers misclassify signals, and how short can a glance be before accurate detection breaks down?

Practical application: Data collected from this experiment can inform machine learning models embedded in automotive systems, enabling better accessibility features for CVD drivers and safety interventions for distracted drivers.

Research Questions & Hypotheses

What We Set Out to Answer

RQ1 — Color Vision Deficiency

What is the lowest severity of deuteranomaly that allows participants to accurately respond whether they should "go" or "brake" when presented red, yellow, or green traffic signals in a simulated driving task in which deuteranomaly varies?

RQ2 — Glance Time

What is the shortest glance time that allows participants to accurately respond to traffic signals in a simulated driving task in which glance time varies and deuteranomaly is held constant?

Null Hypothesis (H₀₁)

Mild deuteranomaly will not prevent participants from accurately perceiving traffic signals.

Null Hypothesis (H₀₂)

The shortest accurate glance time will not be 400ms.

Alternative Hypothesis (Hₖ₁)

Mild deuteranomaly will prevent accurate traffic signal perception.

Alternative Hypothesis (Hₖ₂)

The shortest accurate glance time will be 400ms.

Study Design

Two Independent Conditions

ConditionIndependent VariableHeld ConstantStimuli Per Condition
Condition 1Severity of deuteranomaly (normal → deuteranopia)Glance time10 red × 20 uses  +  10 green × 20 uses
Condition 2Glance time (200ms → 500ms)Deuteranomaly severity10 red × 20 uses  +  10 green × 20 uses

Dependent variable: Participant's binary response indicating whether they would proceed through the traffic signal (G: go) or stop (B: brake).

Methods

Participants, Stimuli & Procedure

Participants

College students with corrected or normal vision and no pre-existing colorblindness. This allowed CVD conditions to be simulated in a controlled way without the confound of genuine individual differences in color vision.

Stimuli

A total of 20 base stimuli were sourced from the Elk Penguin traffic light image dataset: 10 red signal images and 10 green signal images. CVD filters were applied via Colblindor to simulate varying levels of deuteranomaly and deuteranopia. Each of the 10 red stimuli was used 20 times per condition, and each of the 10 green stimuli was used 20 times per condition.

Procedure

01
Random stimulus presentation
02
Participant records G or B
03
Repeat across all stimuli
04
Data recorded & analyzed

Stimuli were presented via PowerPoint with responses manually recorded per stimulus. Trials were presented in random order across both conditions.

Planned Analysis

How the Data Will Be Analyzed

Correlation Analysis

Assess whether deuteranomaly severity and glance time are significantly correlated with traffic signal response accuracy.

t-Tests

Compare the frequency of go vs. brake responses as a function of glance time duration and deuteranomaly severity level.

Potential Confounds

  • Individual differences in visual perception sensitivity
  • Variability in laptop display specifications (luminance, contrast, color gamut)
Theoretical Framework

Why This Matters

Signal Detection Theory (SDT) provides the analytical backbone for this study. By framing participant responses as hits and false alarms, we can compute sensitivity (d') and decision criterion (c) across CVD severity levels and glance durations.

Prior literature establishes that both deuteranomaly and shortened glance time independently degrade signal detection. This study aims to identify the threshold at which each variable alone causes performance to break down, with the longer term goal of informing ML-driven automotive accessibility systems.
